detail.longDescription: Image from <https://gen-ai.fr/blog/atelier/large-language-model/interieur-llm-comprendre-tokens/>. I currently stumble accross how lexeme (like a word, an abstract unit of meaning) are composed morpheme (smallest meaningful constituent of a linguistic expression, especially within a word. ex: the word "unbelievable" is composed of the morpheme "un" + "believ" + "able" ). LLM and AI use token (kinda similar to morpheme, but a bit different) except that tokens seem to be created by the most common group of char/string ( Byte-pair encoding to be more precise ) generated from big corpus of text. (Note: I will use the words token/morpheme interchangeably, speaking loosely) One consequence of that is that common char like space (generally used as a separator in most case) are merged with others char that don't seem to make meaningful token. I do reduce the number of overall tokens / characters (useful for compression), but why it is acceptable to have fewer tokens, my first thought was to have better token/morpheme, ie I mean having less morphene, but those morphene are way more used frequently and make more sens from a grammatical/structure pov. Here is an example to illustrate what I mean : I run some hand made algo to do some byte pair encoding on some english text, the most used tokens/morphemes that I found are : 12175 different kind of Morphemes: (space was NOT forced to be a single morpheme) // "<morpheme> : x<frequency> in the text ", " : x4987 "the " : x4118 "to " : x3973 "and " : x3912 "s " : x3758 " // new line " : x3535 "ed " : x3121 " " : x2921 "that " : x2779 "of " : x2766 "my " : x2766 "not " : x2744 "it " : x2637 "is " : x2562 "in " : x2550 "I " : x2530 "s, " : x2477 "in" : x2468 ". " : x2449 ". // new line then dot " : x2429 ", and " : x2353 " the " : x2331 "ing" : x2246 ... The most common morpheme seem to have a poor quality since the algo don't know that space is a separator. But when I force the space char to be a single morpheme, ie the space morpheme was NOT mergeable with other morpheme / bytes pair I got : 9148 different kind of Morphemes (forcing space) " " : x829308 // forced to be a single morpheme "the" : x24941 "and" : x19364 "to" : x17197 "of" : x16865 "I" : x16356 "a" : x14175 "in" : x11978 "my" : x11321 "you" : x10432 "," : x9433 "is" : x8994 "that" : x8203 "not" : x7876 "with" : x7384 "." : x7318 "be" : x7235 "his" : x6836 "it" : x6669 "me" : x6476 "for" : x6296 "your" : x6276 "have" : x5580 "this" : x5413 ... The quality and frequence of morpheme in this case seem better, and more logical. Note that when forcing space to be a single token/morpheme, I got 24% less morphemes to encode the text, and most notably, the most used morphene got way better frequency. ("the" : x 24941 vs "the " : x 4118, ie: 5 time more usage when I force the space char ). (I think I might use this property to detect punctuation / delimiter ). Why do the algo that generate the tokens ID/indice don't account for stuff like this. I don't mean to force the space char to be a separator, but I mean it's possible to automaticaly detect some morpheme (space or more complicate / composed one) that act like separator ? Why do it prefer having more token ID, even if they are less frequently used ? (Note the algo was trained locally on The Complete Works of William Shakespeare by William Shakespeare ) Ps: I'm still new to all of this. I know more about writing parsers and having an interest in linguistics than having deep knowledge about AI.
